messages.subject: Re: Error in seq.default(from = 1, to = CNt, by = 1) : 'to' cannot be NA, NaN or infinite
messages.subject_clean: Error in seq.default(from = 1, to = CNt, by = 1) : 'to' cannot be NA, NaN or infinite
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I ran into similar problem, and i found out that sequenza does not like chromosomes being not in reference order. I spent two days figuring. I think it is sequenza bug.

E. g. if i convert bam2seqz in parallel and then merge results as advised:

sequenza-utils.py bam2seqz --parallel 8 -C chr1 chr2 chr3 chr4 chr5 chr6 chr7 chr8 chr9 chr10 chr11 chr12 chr13 chr14 chr15 chr16 chr17 chr18 chr19 chr20 chr21 chr22 chrX chrY chrM -n normal.bam -t tumor.bam --fasta hg38.analysisSet.fa -gc hg38.gc50Base.wig.gz -o out.seqz.gz

zcat *.seqz.gz | gawk '{if (NR!=1 && $1 != "chromosome") {print $0}}' | bgzip > out.seqz.gz

, then chromosomes will follow in lexicographical order:

chr1 chr10 chr11 chr12 chr13 chr14 chr15 chr16 chr17 chr18 chr19 chr2 chr20 chr21 chr22 chr3 chr4 chr5 chr6 chr7 chr8 chr9 chrM chrX chrY

, and sequenza fit gives the error (and also the first line in the result is lost).

So now i place chromosomes in the reference order:

chr1 chr2 chr3 chr4 chr5 chr6 chr7 chr8 chr9 chr10 chr11 chr12 chr13 chr14 chr15 chr16 chr17 chr18 chr19 chr20 chr21 chr22 chrX chrY chrM

CHROMOSOMES=`awk 'BEGIN{c="chr"; for (a=1; a <= 22; a++) print c a}'`" chrX chrY chrM"
CHR_FILES=`echo $CHROMOSOMES  | sed 's/\s\+/\n/g' | awk '{print "out_" $0 ".seqz.gz"}'`
zcat $CHR_FILES | gawk -v SEQ_HEADER="`zcat $CHR_FILES | head -n 1`" 'BEGIN{print SEQ_HEADER} {if (NR!=1 && $1 != "chromosome") {print $0}}' | bgzip > out.seqz.gz
tabix -f -s 1 -b 2 -e 2 -S 1 out.seqz.gz

And sequenza runs perfectly fine despite the data being basically the same!

I think at least the above script should be part of the original bam2seqz in parallel mode. And at most there should be detailed investigation, whether this bug affects validity of sequenza results even when this error does not occur. Unfortunately i can not make this investigation cos i basically have no clue what sequenza does. :'(

> data.file = "out.small.seqz.gz"
>
> # out.small.seqz.gz is generated by sequenza-utils.py

> CP.example = sequenza.fit(seqzdata)
>
> sequenza.results(sequenza.extract = seqzdata , cp.table = CP.example, sample.id <http://sample.id> = "C0053", out.dir="/path/to/outdir/sequenza")
>

> Error in seq.default(from = 1, to = CNt, by = 1) :
>   'to' cannot be NA, NaN or infinite

>   no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf
>
> Is tehre any recomemndation to solve this error?
>
> Thanks,
> Amit

messages.body_plain:
I actually discovered the root of the problem (at least in my case). https://bitbucket.org/sequenzatools/sequenza/issues/19/error-in-seqdefault-finite-number-issue

1. I included chrM in my chromosome list.
2. chrM is only about 17k long.
3. windowValues function can not properly handle such short intervals so it gives NA in chrM_ratio$chrM$end (and maybe there are other similar errors but this error comes first).
4. sequenza.results processes only 24 first chromosomes by default.
5. So when my chromosomes come in lexicographical order, it takes chrM, and when they are in reference order, chrM is 25th chromosome so it is ignored.

So basically it means that sequenza was not made to process chrM, and it should not be given to sequenza input. However i think sequenza should warn me about this rather than telling me magical curse words.
